summary: Generalised tripwires caught 10 of 16 promise-concern PRs (missed 6; any contract tripped on 14); 33 of 60 ordinary merged PRs tripped a promise contract (noise 55%); strict 2025 paths: caught 4, noise 18 of 60

missed.title: Secure by default
missed.why: Behavioural default flip: one line in src/MessagePack/MessagePackSerializerOptions.cs makes UntrustedData the default security policy. No contract path or pattern covers option defaults; the security contract names only SECURITY.md and MessagePackSecurity.cs. Only README/doc (user-docs) tripped.

missed.title: Performance/1807 force method inline
missed.why: Labelled 'generated' because the maintainer said to edit the .tt and regenerate, but the files are the library's own T4 output (MessagePackReader.Integers.cs etc.), not code generated into the consumer's assembly. It tripped wire-format (MessagePackReader.cs by file name), so it would have been shown; the miss is a label/contract mismatch.

missed.title: Move BuildTypeName() from TypelessFormatter to MessagePackSerializerOptions
missed.why: Moves a member from TypelessFormatter to MessagePackSerializerOptions without updating PublicAPI.*.txt, so public-api cannot see it; it did trip wire-format (Formatters/TypelessFormatter.cs), so the owner would still have been shown it, under the wrong contract.

missed.title: Handle DataContract(Order=N) across class hierarchies?
missed.why: Wire compatibility break through member-ordering logic in Resolvers/DynamicObjectResolver.cs (DataContract Order across a hierarchy). The wire-format contract names reader/writer/code/formatter files, not the dynamic resolver that decides key order. Nothing tripped.

missed.title: Enable support for platforms (e.g. Blazor WASM) where System.Reflection.Emit is not supported.
missed.why: Field-to-property change on MessagePackSerializerOptions is binary breaking, but the PR edits only MessagePackSerializerOptions.cs and does not touch PublicAPI.*.txt; a one-line .cs change is invisible to paths and patterns. Nothing tripped.

missed.title: Avoid `MissingMethodException` on generic classes with `init` property setters
missed.why: Behavioural compat change (throw instead of quietly returning null for init-only setters on generic types) inside Resolvers/DynamicObjectResolver.cs, which no contract names. Only README (user-docs) tripped.

method.positives: history.json PRs with concern in public-api, wire-format, generated, targets, diagnostics, security, compat-breaking; head = refs/pr/N fetched from https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp pull/N/head (final PR head, i.e. after any review changes).
method.positive_base:
Merged PR with a merge commit on record: merge-base with that merge's first parent (the
branch it landed on). Otherwise: merge-base with whichever upstream line in BASE_CANDIDATES
is closest to the head (fewest head-only commits). A line that already contains the head
(PR merged there but no merge commit recorded) is resolved to the first merge on that line's
first-parent history that brought the head in, and that merge's first parent is used.
method.reverted_cross_check: for reverted PRs the original commit recorded in history.json is also diffed against its first parent (generalised matcher) and reported beside the PR-head result; the PR-head result is the one scored.
method.controls: `git log --merges --first-parent 32258fdb`, subjects 'Merge pull request #N from <branch>' only; drop PRs whose number appears anywhere in history.json; drop by branch regex /dependabot/|libtemplate|Library\.Template|renovate// or title (first body line) regex /^\s*(bump|dependency updates)\b|^\s*merge\b(.*\b(to|into)\s+(master|develop|v\d\S*)\s*$|\s+latest\b)|^\s*update\b.*\b(sdk|packages?|dependenc(y|ies)|references)\b|dependabot|renovate|library\.template|\bsdk\b|\bci\b|github actions|azure pipelines?|codecov|\b(master|develop)\s+(to|into)\s+(master|develop)\b|^\s*build\b|\bbuild (script|tasks?|artifact)|\bunity build\b|\bpackage dependenc/ (case-insensitive); keep only the years the positives span; 60 picked with an equal share per year (a year with too few PRs passes its unused share on), evenly spaced by date within a year. Diff = <merge>^1..<merge>.
method.diff: git diff -U0 --no-renames (a moved file counts as delete + add). Deleted files are matched on their old path; tripwires.py currently drops deleted files (it keys hunks on the +++ path), so a pure deletion of a contract file would not trip there.
method.strict_rule: exactly tripwires.py: hunk file under a contract path (prefix for dirs, equality for files), or a changed (+/-) line in a file not under tests/ matching a contract line pattern.
generalised_rule: A hunk trips contract C when any of these holds:
otherwise only for product files, i.e. no directory segment named sandbox/benchmark(s)/perf/sample(s) or containing a 'test'/'tests'/'unittests' dotted component (e.g. tests/, MessagePack.Tests/):
(2) a directory segment equals the last segment of one of C's directory paths (Formatters, Transforms, Analyzers, CodeAnalysis, analyzers);

(3) the file name equals the file name of one of C's file paths (PublicAPI.Shipped.txt, PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt, MessagePackReader.cs, SECURITY.md, ...) or of a file inside one of C's directory paths at base, counting only file names that are unique in the base tree and not dotfiles (so FormatterTemplate.tt or StandardClassLibraryFormatter.cs match in any layout, .editorconfig does not);

(4) a changed line matches one of C's line patterns, plus, for each csproj/props line C cites in `sources`, the XML element on that line in singular or plural form (targets: <TargetFrameworks?>), in any file.
No per-era path is listed by hand; everything comes from project.json and the base tree.
method.caught_definition: caught = the generalised tripped set includes at least one contract mapped from the PR's concern; missed otherwise.
method.noise_definition: noise = share of control PRs whose tripped set includes any of public-api, wire-format, generated, targets, diagnostics, security; user-docs is reported separately and not counted as noise.

limits: Tripping is not a verdict. The real gate also needs a check that the promise actually changed (PublicAPI diff, byte round-trip, regenerated output, TFM list). A trip only says 'show the owner'; a high trip rate on controls means owner time, not wrong answers.
Small sample: 16 positives and 60 controls. One PR moves the catch rate by about 6 points.

Concern labels came from an agent reading maintainer comments via WebFetch (history.json, produced_by hand); some quotes are fragments and some PR pages were only partly read. A wrong label moves a PR between caught and missed.
Positives are diffed at the final PR head. For merged-after-changes PRs that is after the maintainer's requested fixes, which can remove (or add) the very change that drew the concern.

Controls are merged PRs with no recorded pushback in history.json, but history.json was built from targeted searches, so some controls may also have had review pushback we could not see (api.github.com is blocked). Noise is therefore an upper bound on 'trips nobody needed'.
Controls come from the develop first-parent line only; PRs that landed on master/v1.x/v2.x are not sampled.

Older layouts (Unity client shared sources, mpc GeneratorCore, MessagePackAnalyzer) only match where a base-tree file name or directory name survived; renamed files and directories are invisible to the rule by design.
The contracts are the 2025 ones; promises the project made in 2019-2021 (e.g. v1 binary compatibility, mpc tool targets) are only covered as far as the 2025 contracts happen to describe them.
